title: Isandro and the Summer
premise: Ulyana Fairweather inherited her grandmother's vineyard along with its crushing debts, and has spent two summers pretending the estate is thriving. When her family reunion looms, she hires Isandro, a quiet seasonal worker with a talent for listening, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real, but Isandro is guarding his own secret: he was sent by the vineyard's creditors to assess whether the property is worth saving. As the summer festival approaches and the last train of the season becomes a deadline, Ulyana must choose between the comfortable lie of solitude and a love that demands truth. In the end, Isandro betrays his employers to testify on her behalf, the vineyard is saved through an unexpected cooperative of townspeople, and he stays past the last train, choosing her over the life he was sent back to.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former sommelier who abandoned the restaurant world to write love stories set among vines and small-town secrets. He lives off-season in a coastal village where the trains stop running in October.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She walks the failing vineyard at dawn, tallying what she owes against what the vines can give, and learns the reunion invitation requires a plus-one. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the armor of routine cracking under family pressure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixed the Trellis
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He arrives as a seasonal hire, quietly cataloging the estate's value for the creditors who sent him, but finds himself repairing a broken trellis Ulyana couldn't afford to fix. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as diligence, first flicker of attachment.

chapters.title: Terms of the Arrangement
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Over cheap wine in the cellar, she proposes the fake relationship; Isandro agrees too quickly, and both pretend it's a simple transaction. Emotional beat: nervous comedy shading into an unspoken hunger neither will name.

chapters.title: The Reunion, Act One
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating scenes. The family descends, probing Ulyana's failures, and Isandro performs the devoted boyfriend with unsettling sincerity. Emotional beat: the lie working too well, Ulyana's terror at how easily she believes it.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. After the reunion dinner, they escape to the orchard and nearly kiss, then retreat into bickering about nothing. Isandro's phone buzzes with his handler's message, unseen. Emotional beat: longing interrupted by the first shadow of his secret.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He files a preliminary report recommending seizure, then finds Ulyana's grandmother's letters revealing the debts were a predatory loan, not mismanagement. Emotional beat: conscience waking, loyalty to his mission beginning to rot.

chapters.title: The Festival Opens
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The town's summer festival begins; Ulyana publicly thanks Isandro, and the crowd's warmth makes his deception unbearable. His handler arrives in person, demanding final numbers by the festival's end. Emotional beat: the walls closing in, tenderness curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Truth, Spilled Like Wine
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax part one. She discovers his report and his employer's letter; the confrontation in the cellar strips away every tender moment they faked and every real one they denied. Emotional beat: betrayal, rage, and the terrible admission that she loves him anyway.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, climax part two. He chooses: he delivers testimony exposing the predatory loan to the town assembly instead of the creditors, burning his career. As the last train of the season prepares to leave, he stands on the platform deciding. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the terror of hoping.

chapters.title: Staying After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, resolution. The townspeople form a cooperative to buy out the debt; the vineyard's first honest harvest begins. Isandro walks up the road with his single bag as the train departs empty behind him. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love in the present tense at last.
